findings.title: How a North Korean Fake IT Worker Tried to Infiltrate Us
findings.summary_md: KnowBe4 published a first-person account of nearly hiring an operative operating under a stolen US identity for a remote AI engineering role. The new hire attempted to load malware onto the company-issued laptop during onboarding, minutes after receiving it. The incident became the reference case for DPRK operatives seeking remote jobs at Western companies, predating this story by more than two years.

findings.title: US offers $5 million for info on North Korean IT worker farms
findings.summary_md: The State Department offered a reward of up to $5 million through its Rewards for Justice program for information that could disrupt the activities of North Korean IT worker farms. The offer, made in December 2024, framed the farms as revenue generation for the regime and invited reporting on facilitators inside the United States.

findings.title: Jasper Sleet: North Korean remote IT workers' evolving tactics to infiltrate organizations
findings.summary_md: Microsoft detailed the tactics of the Jasper Sleet activity set, its tracking name for DPRK remote IT worker operations, including the laptop farm model and the use of deepfakes in job interviews. The writeup documents how operatives convert a fraudulent hire into persistent access to the employer's environment and payroll.

findings.title: US sanctions North Korea IT worker networks in Laos, Vietnam
findings.summary_md: The US Treasury sanctioned North Korean IT worker networks operating out of Laos and Vietnam, targeting the overseas infrastructure that places operatives into remote jobs at Western companies. The action was part of a sustained enforcement run against the scheme through 2025 and 2026.

findings.title: 11 nations issue first-ever joint alert on North Korean IT worker schemes
findings.summary_md: Eleven nations jointly issued the first coordinated alert on North Korean IT worker schemes, warning companies about fraudulent remote employment pipelines. The alert was published in August 2026, two months before the Justice Department announced Operation Lonestar Roundup.
